review_policy: reviewed means every capture cited for the operation replays against the node with no difference and at least one is cited, for the cases those captures cover; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a difference a replay observes, and the capture's replay lists it exactly. not_reviewed means the cited captures, if any, don't settle the operation, even if the node routes it.

deliberate_gaps.timestamped-signatures-only: Every signed operation: upstream also accepts a request whose auth chain signs only its method and its path below /v1 (lowercased), whatever x-identity-timestamp or x-identity-metadata header the request carries or omits, valid until the delegated key expires. The node accepts only the timestamped payload over its own method and path, at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses such a request with upstream's 401 {ok:false, data:{message}, error:'Unauthenticated'}.
deliberate_gaps.signature-window: Every signed operation: upstream accepts a timestamp up to 30 minutes old or ahead; the node accepts at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses the rest with the same 401.
deliberate_gaps.unauthenticated-message: Every signed operation: when a signature does not verify, upstream's data.message is its verifier's own text, which includes the payload it expected and its local clock; the node's is a fixed text naming the failed check (Invalid auth chain, Invalid timestamp, Expired signature, Invalid signature). The status, error and envelope are upstream's, and no client reads data.message.
deliberate_gaps.chain-copy-lag: Every operation that reads a collection's published or approved state: upstream asks the Polygon collections subgraph on each request; the node reads its copy of that subgraph, which the shop's collections mirror refreshes every three times MARKETPLACE_MIRROR_INTERVAL_SECS (15 minutes at the default 300). A collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow reads as unpublished, and an approval or a role change as not yet made, until the next pass, so a client that polls after a deployment (the old builder web retries its publish every 5 seconds) waits up to that bound plus the subgraph's lag. When the copy has no complete pass the node answers 503, and when its last pass, or the row or absence a decision reads, is more than 30 minutes old it answers 503 to every request that grants access or writes.

operations.result: The owner's reads of a draft, a published unapproved and a published approved collection, the unsigned refusal, a stranger's refusal and each signature refusal were compared; the signature refusals are re-signed at replay time with their defect, so each reaches the check it names. The refusals answer upstream's status and envelope; the owner's reads answer upstream's is_published and is_approved and differ in other fields, and a request signed over method and path alone is refused where upstream serves it.

evidence.scope: Signed GET by the owner of a draft standard collection.
Signed GET by the owner of a standard collection the collections subgraph holds as not approved; the replay seeds the same facts into the node's copy of the subgraph.
Signed GET by the owner of a standard collection the collections subgraph holds as approved; the replay seeds the same facts into the node's copy of the subgraph.
GET without an auth chain.
Signed GET by a wallet with no role on the draft.
GET whose first auth chain header is not JSON; replayed with its recorded headers.
GET signed by the owner 40 minutes before the request; re-signed at replay time 40 minutes before the replay, so the window check refuses it.
GET signed by the owner 40 minutes after the request; re-signed at replay time 40 minutes ahead, so the future bound refuses it.
GET signed by the owner over another collection path; re-signed at replay time over that path, so the signature check refuses it.
GET whose x-identity-metadata is not the metadata the owner signed; re-signed at replay time with the same mismatch, so the signature check refuses it.
GET signed by the owner with {"signer":"decentraland-kernel-scene"} metadata; re-signed for the replay.
GET signed by the owner with {"Signer":"dcl:explorer"} metadata; re-signed for the replay.
GET signed by the owner over get:/collections/{id} alone, with no timestamp or metadata header, as the old builder web signs; re-signed at replay time with a live delegated key.
GET signed by the owner as a PUT; re-signed at replay time with the other method, so the signature check refuses it.
GET signed by the owner over get:/collections/{id} alone but sent with a current timestamp and {} metadata; re-signed at replay time with a live delegated key.

The node creates the draft with a different body, refuses the untimestamped request, refuses the invalid body with upstream's status and error, and refuses the unsigned one before reading its body, as upstream does.

evidence.scope: Signed PUT by the owner creating a new standard draft with a client-shaped body (eth_address set to the signer, data set). created_at and updated_at come from the database clock and are volatile.
PUT signed by the owner over put:/collections/{id} alone, with no timestamp or metadata header, as the old builder web signs; re-signed at replay time with a live delegated key.
Signed PUT by the owner whose collection name is a number; re-signed for the replay.
PUT without a signature whose collection name is a number: both refuse it as unauthenticated before validating the body.

gaps: Create: upstream stores the salt and the contract address it computes from the id and data and answers them with the collection urn; the node answers contract_address and urn as null and omits salt, managers, minters, reviewed_at, forum_link, forum_id, lock, linked_contract_address, linked_contract_network, is_mapping_complete and item_count, and adds third_party_id. The timestamps are volatile in this capture, so their format is compared by the owner read of GET /v1/collections/:id.
Invalid body: both answer 400 {ok:false, data, error:'Invalid request body'}; upstream's data lists its JSON schema errors, the node's is {}.
operations.remaining_verification: Capture an update of an existing draft, a third-party collection, a locked and a published collection (423 and 409 upstream), a name already in use, a stranger's write and mismatched body and URL ids.
